name: Sreevallabha Temple, Thiruvalla
deity: Vishnu as Sreevallabha, 'beloved of Sri' — Kolappiran of the hymns — standing in four-armed form
period: A Divya Desam of Malai Nadu, sung by Nammalvar and Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At Thiruvalla, Vishnu is worshipped as Sreevallabha, beloved of Lakshmi — a Malai Nadu Divya Desam sung by Nammalvar and Thirumangai Alvar, where Kathakali is offered to the lord as worship.

sections.history: Thiruvalla — the Thiruvalvazh of the hymns — is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and a principal shrine of Malai Nadu; Nammalvar and Thirumangai Alvar both sang its lord, whom they called Kolappiran, 'the lord of beauty'. The temple's medieval importance is recorded in the Thiruvalla copper plates, a long grant of the Chera era that sets out lands and endowments for its worship. The town grew up around the shrine, and Sreevallabha remained at the heart of its life through the centuries of the Kerala kingdoms that followed.
sections.architecture: Built in the Kerala manner, the temple gathers its sanctum (srikovil) within the nalambalam cloister and a broad walled compound. Before it rises a tall Garuda pillar carved from a single stone and crowned by the figure of Garuda, Vishnu's eagle mount — one of the temple's great landmarks. Murals adorn the walls of the sanctum, and a Kathakali stage stands before the eastern entrance.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of a devout woman who kept the Ekadashi vow faithfully and longed to feed a brahmachari when it ended. The asura Thukalasura troubled the land, and Vishnu sent his discus Sudarshana to destroy him; then the lord himself came in the form of a young brahmachari to accept her offering. The god who came for love of a devotee of Sri is honoured here as Sreevallabha, and the discus Sudarshana, in the lord's raised hand, recalls the weapon that set the land free.
sections.festivals: The annual utsavam is celebrated with flag hoisting and processions, and Vaikunta Ekadashi draws devotees from across central Travancore. Kathakali performances, staged almost daily before the eastern entrance and offered as worship by devotees are a living part of the temple's ritual life, and on festival nights the drums and lamps of the dance-drama carry on long into the dark.
sections.experience: Arrive in the evening if you can, when the lamps are lit around the compound and a Kathakali performance may be offered to the lord. Spend a moment before the great Garuda pillar, look for the murals around the sanctum, and recall the Alvars who sang the beauty of Kolappiran in Tamil far from this Malayalam-speaking town.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan and a midday closure, following the temple's own schedule; festival days are crowded. Confirm current timings locally before you visit.
visit.dressCode: Traditional dress is expected: by Kerala temple custom men usually enter bare-chested in a mundu or dhoti, and women in saree or other traditional dress; footwear is left outside. Follow posted rules and the guidance of temple staff.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted in and around the sanctum; follow posted rules and the guidance of temple staff.
visit.gettingThere: The temple is in Thiruvalla town, Pathanamthitta district. Thiruvalla railway station lies on the Ernakulam–Kottayam–Kollam line, the town is on the Main Central (MC) Road, and Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram have the nearest airports.
